chapters.title: Chapter 2: What You Give Up and What You Keep

lessons.title: HRA, LTA and Home Loan Interest: Exemptions That Disappear in the New Regime

children.text: The last lesson ended with a hard fact: even maxing out 80C, NPS and 80D saves at most ₹85,800. If the old regime is going to beat the new one, the heavy lifting usually comes from two places: the rent you pay and the home loan you repay. This lesson shows you exactly how much each one is worth, and what happens to it in the new regime.

body.text: HRA and home loan interest are the two benefits big enough to swing the regime decision. If you have neither, the old regime almost never wins.

children.text: House Rent Allowance: The Least of Three

markDefs.definition: For HRA purposes, basic salary plus dearness allowance (DA) that forms part of retirement benefits. Bonuses and other allowances are excluded.

children.text: HRA is the allowance in your salary meant for rent. Under the old regime, part of it is exempt under the salary exemption rules (Section 10(13A) of the 1961 Act). The exempt amount is the lowest of three numbers, all calculated on an annual basis using your
for the months you actually lived in rented housing.

body.latex: \text{HRA exempt} = \min\Big(\text{HRA received},\; \text{Rent paid} - 10\%\text{ of salary},\; 50\%\text{ or } 40\%\text{ of salary}\Big)
body.caption: 50% of salary if you rent in a metro city, 40% elsewhere. Salary means basic plus DA. Whatever HRA is not exempt is taxed as part of your salary.
Arvind in Indore: Basic ₹40,000, HRA ₹16,000, Rent ₹15,000 (All Monthly)

body.text: For the 50% limit, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai have historically been the only metro cities. A Bengaluru, Hyderabad or Pune renter has used the 40% limit, despite metro-level rents. Check the current Income-tax Rules for the tax year you are filing, because this list has been proposed for expansion.

body.title: Calculate Sneha's HRA Exemption
body.prompt: Sneha rents a flat in Delhi's Lajpat Nagar. Her basic salary is ₹50,000 a month, her HRA is ₹25,000 a month and she pays rent of ₹22,000 a month. She has no DA. What is her annual HRA exemption?
body.explanation: Actual HRA is ₹3,00,000. Rent minus 10% of salary is ₹2,64,000 minus ₹60,000, which is ₹2,04,000. 50% of salary for a metro is ₹3,00,000. The lowest is ₹2,04,000. At the 30% slab, that exemption saves her ₹63,648 including cess in the old regime.

body.title: Sneha's HRA Exemption at Different Monthly Rents (₹ Thousand a Year)

children.text: Notice the flat top. Every extra ₹5,000 of monthly rent adds ₹60,000 of exemption, until the exemption hits her ₹3 lakh HRA ceiling at ₹30,000 rent. Beyond that, paying more rent buys no more tax benefit. Your HRA exemption can never exceed the HRA your employer actually pays you.

body.text: Fake rent receipts are one of the most common reasons salaried employees get tax notices. If annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh, you must give your employer the landlord's PAN, and the department can cross-check that PAN against the landlord's return. Paying genuine rent to your parents is allowed if they own the house and declare the rent as income. Rent paid to your spouse generally does not pass scrutiny.

children.text: No HRA in your salary? Freelancers and employees without an HRA component can claim a smaller rent deduction under Section 80GG of the 1961 Act, capped at ₹5,000 a month. It is also old regime only.
Leave Travel Allowance: Two Trips in Four Years

LTA (Section 10(5) of the 1961 Act) exempts what your employer reimburses for domestic travel on leave. The rules are narrow: only travel within India, only the fare (economy air, AC first class rail or equivalent), not hotels, food or sightseeing, and only two journeys in a block of four calendar years. Your spouse, children and dependent parents travelling with you are covered.

body.label: Current LTA block
body.context: Two exempt journeys allowed in this block. An unused journey from the 2022 to 2025 block can be carried into calendar year 2026.

body.title: What Does LTA Cover?
body.question: Aditi's employer gives her ₹60,000 of LTA. She spends ₹28,000 on return economy flights from Mumbai to Kochi for herself and her husband, ₹35,000 on a houseboat stay, and ₹8,000 on local taxis. It is her first LTA claim of the 2026 to 2029 block. How much is exempt under the old regime?
body.explanation: Only the travel fare between origin and destination qualifies. The ₹28,000 of flights is exempt. The houseboat stay and local taxis are not, so the remaining ₹32,000 of LTA is taxable.

children.text: Home Loan Interest: The Only One With a Twist

Home loans give you two separate benefits. The principal repaid counts towards the ₹1.5 lakh 80C bucket, now Section 123. The interest paid is deducted from income from house property under Section 22 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 24(b) of the 1961 Act). What happens to the interest depends on whether you live in the house or rent it out, and this is the one benefit that does not disappear completely in the new regime.

body.title: Home Loan Interest: Self-Occupied vs Let-Out

columns.label: House you live in (self-occupied)
points: Old regime: interest deductible up to ₹2,00,000 a year
Creates a house property loss that is set off against your salary
Interest paid before construction finished is claimed in 5 equal yearly parts, within the ₹2 lakh cap
New regime: no deduction at all

columns.label: House you rent out (let-out)
points: Both regimes: full interest deductible against the rent you earn
Old regime: a resulting loss can be set off against salary up to ₹2,00,000, and the rest carried forward for 8 years
New regime: the loss cannot be set off against salary and cannot be carried forward
In practice the new regime lets interest reduce rental income to zero, but not below

children.text: Pooja, a Bengaluru-based HR manager, owns a flat in Pune that she rents out for ₹25,000 a month. She pays ₹12,000 of municipal tax and ₹4,50,000 of home loan interest in the year. Here is her house property income in each regime.

body.caption: Pooja's Let-Out Flat in Pune, Tax Year 2026-27

cells: Set off against salary this year

body.text: In the new regime, Pooja's rent is still fully cancelled by her interest, so she pays no tax on the ₹3 lakh rent. What she loses is the extra ₹2 lakh reduction in her salary income. At the 30% slab that is worth ₹62,400 a year, and the ₹48,400 carry-forward disappears too.

body.title: Rahul and Nisha's Joint Home Loan
body.scenario: Rahul and Nisha, both software engineers in Noida, bought a flat together that they live in. They are equal co-owners and co-borrowers on an SBI home loan. This year they paid ₹3,80,000 of interest and ₹1,40,000 of principal, split equally from their own salaries. Each earns ₹22 lakh, and neither has any HRA since they own their home.
body.prompt: How much home loan benefit can each claim under the old regime, and what changes if they move to the new regime?
body.modelAnswer: Because they are both co-owners and co-borrowers, and each pays their share, each can claim separately. Each paid ₹1,90,000 of interest, which is within the ₹2 lakh self-occupied cap, so each deducts ₹1,90,000 under Section 22 (24(b)). Each also paid ₹70,000 of principal, which counts towards their own ₹1.5 lakh 80C bucket under Section 123. At the 30% slab, the interest deduction alone saves each of them ₹59,280 including cess. Had the loan been in Rahul's name alone, he could only have claimed ₹2 lakh of the ₹3.8 lakh interest. In the new regime, both deductions vanish because the house is self-occupied, so each must compare that loss against the new regime's lower slabs before deciding.

body.title: The New Regime Rule for Let-Out Property
body.textWithBlank: In the new regime, a loss from a let-out house property can be neither set off against salary nor carried ___.
body.explanation: The new regime still allows interest on a let-out property to reduce rental income, but any resulting loss simply lapses. In the old regime, up to ₹2 lakh is set off against other income and the rest can be carried forward for 8 years.

body.caption: Summary: What Each Benefit Is Worth and Where It Survives
headers: Typical size for a metro salaried employee

cells: ₹1.5 lakh to ₹6 lakh, depending on rent and HRA
Fare for two trips per four-year block
Only against rent, no loss set-off

body.title: Gather Your Rent and Home Loan Numbers
steps: Note your monthly basic salary, DA and HRA from your payslip
Total the rent you actually paid this tax year and keep the rent agreement handy
Collect your landlord's PAN if annual rent is above ₹1 lakh
Run the least-of-three HRA formula using 50% or 40% based on your city
Download your home loan interest certificate and split interest from principal
If the property is let out, note rent received and municipal taxes paid

points: HRA exemption is the lowest of HRA received, rent minus 10% of salary, and 50% (metro) or 40% (non-metro) of salary.
Your HRA exemption can never exceed the HRA your employer pays, so rent above a certain level adds no benefit.
LTA covers only domestic travel fares, for two journeys in each four-year block, currently 2026 to 2029.
Self-occupied home loan interest of up to ₹2 lakh is deductible only in the old regime.
Let-out property interest still reduces rental income in the new regime, but the resulting loss cannot be set off or carried forward.
HRA, home loan interest, LTA and 80GG all vanish in the new regime, and they are usually what decides whether the old regime can win.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not tax advice. Rules reflect tax year 2026-27 as understood at the time of writing. Salary exemption provisions and the metro city list under the Income-tax Act, 2025 and its Rules should be confirmed against the official text. Consult a qualified tax professional before filing.
